questions.q: Which set best describes what makes up a model version in this lesson?
options: The file plus its content hash, the training data hash, the settings and library versions, and the metrics
Only the .joblib file and its file name
Only the metrics
Only the Git commit message
questions.explain: A version is the file plus enough metadata to identify it, reproduce it and judge it: hash, data hash, recipe (settings and library versions) and results.

questions.q: In the lesson's demo, training twice with C = 1.0 produced the same model id. What is the right way to interpret this?
options: Every training run in any project is guaranteed to give identical bytes
The hash identifies a specific file; identical bytes here came from a deterministic recipe, but that is not guaranteed in general
Hashes cannot detect changes to a file
It proves the model is accurate
questions.explain: Random elements, multi-threading or different library versions can change the bytes. The hash names a file; the sidecar records how it was made.

questions.q: Why is the metadata sidecar committed to Git while the .joblib file goes through DVC?
options: Git cannot store JSON files
Sidecars must be hidden from teammates
DVC cannot handle text
The sidecar is small plain text that diffs readably, while the model is a binary file that changes on every retrain
questions.explain: Small text files suit Git; large or binary artifacts suit DVC's cache and remote, with a pointer file in Git.

questions.q: What does git tag model-v1 add to the workflow?
options: It trains the model again
It encrypts the model file
A human-readable name for the commit that holds that model's pointer and sidecar
It uploads the model to the DVC remote
questions.explain: Tags give versions memorable names. Checking out the pointer and sidecar from a tag, then running dvc checkout, restores that exact model.

questions.q: What did load_verified do when one extra byte was appended to the model file?
options: It loaded the model silently
It deleted the file
It retrained the model
It raised an error because the recomputed hash no longer matched the sidecar
questions.explain: Recomputing the SHA-256 and comparing it with the sidecar catches corruption or tampering before a pickle is ever loaded.
